scenario.fault_family: routing daemon down (redundancy loss, no user outage)
scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Monitoring raised a fabric alarm: super_spine_router_0 and BOTH leaf
routers each report their BGP session toward spine_router_0_0 going
down within seconds of each other. No user has complained -- pc_0_0
(10.0.0.2) and pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2) still reach each other -- but the
fabric is now running without its usual redundancy. All of
spine_router_0_0's interfaces still show UP. Find what broke.

injection.action: kill the BGP routing daemon (and watchfrr) on spine_router_0_0

post_inject_check.expect: 0% loss   (still OK -- redundant fabric via spine_router_0_1)

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: spine_router_0_0 bgpd
Mechanism: spine_router_0_0 (AS 65100) peers with super_spine_router_0
  (172.16.0.0, AS 65000), leaf_router_0_0 (172.16.0.5, AS 65200) and
  leaf_router_0_1 (172.16.0.7, AS 65201). Killing bgpd tears down all
  three sessions at once (the peers see the TCP session close and fall
  to Idle/Active). The CLOS fabric is redundant: both leaves still peer
  with spine_router_0_1, so 10.0.0.0/24 and 10.0.1.0/24 stay reachable
  via the other spine and users see at most a brief blip. The impact is
  loss of path redundancy, not an outage.
Localization: spine_router_0_0
Root cause: bgpd not running on spine_router_0_0
Fix: restart FRR on spine_router_0_0 (`service frr restart`) -- the
  config persists in /etc/frr/frr.conf, so the restart restores all
  three sessions.

Observable note: bgpd is killed together with watchfrr (its watchdog),
so nothing respawns it (this kill pattern is lab-verified on this
fabric's leaf routers, 2026-07-03; the spines run the same image and
FRR config layout). vtysh remains responsive via zebra,
`show running-config` on spine_router_0_0 simply contains NO
`router bgp` section, and `show daemons` no longer lists bgpd. An agent
may therefore correctly describe this fault as "the bgp configuration
is missing/empty on spine_router_0_0" -- that is the same fault observed
at the config plane, and must NOT be treated as a wrong root cause.
scenario.fix_spec:
`service frr restart` on spine_router_0_0. The persistent
/etc/frr/frr.conf brings bgpd back with its full neighbor configuration;
the sessions to the super-spine and both leaves re-establish and the
fabric regains its second spine path.

bonus-notes-redundancy: explains that reachability survives because spine_router_0_1 still carries both host prefixes (loss of redundancy, not an outage)

agent.diagnosis_text:
**Affected component:** The `bgpd` daemon (and its supervisor `watchfrr`) on `spine_router_0_0` has stopped. Only `zebra` remains running; the BGP control plane is completely absent on this device.

**Mechanism:** BGP sessions are maintained as long-lived TCP connections kept alive by the BGP daemon. When `bgpd` exits, the OS tears down those TCP connections immediately, sending a TCP FIN/RST to each peer. All three peers — `super_spine_router_0`, `leaf_router_0_0`, and `leaf_router_0_1` — received the session teardown at the same moment (within seconds of each other), which is exactly what the fabric alarm described. The simultaneous multi-peer drop is the hallmark of a daemon crash rather than a link, ASN, or policy fault.

**Localization:** `spine_router_0_0` — confirmed by `ps aux` showing no `bgpd` or `watchfrr` process. The peer routers correctly report their session state as `Active` (attempting to reconnect) while their sessions toward `spine_router_0_1` remain `Established`. Data-plane connectivity between `pc_0_0` and `pc_0_1` survived because `spine_router_0_1` provides a full alternate path and its BGP sessions are intact.

**Root cause:** `bgpd` (and the `watchfrr` supervisor) crashed or was killed on `spine_router_0_0`, removing the device's entire BGP control plane and dropping all three of its BGP peering sessions simultaneously.

**Fix:** Restart FRR on `spine_router_0_0` — `systemctl restart frr` — to bring `watchfrr`, `bgpd`, and the full daemon stack back up. Sessions will re-establish automatically once `bgpd` is running and peers reconnect.

The report explicitly states that bgpd (and its supervisor watchfrr) has stopped on spine_router_0_0 and attributes the peer session teardowns to that daemon being down.
